text.p: Nigerian shares on Monday consolidated impressive gains made on the stock exchange last week, traders said.
The all-share index closed at 6422.79 from 6396.45 on Friday.
Construction company Cappa and D'Alberto shares rose by the maximum five percent permitted, after it announced an increase in profits. The stock closed 34 kobo higher at 7.04 naira.
Most blue chips rose on sustained demand. Unipetrol rose 40 kobo to 38.20 naira. National Oil rose 30 kobo to 29.60 naira.
Total, African Petroleum and Mobil were all 20 kobo higher at 45.10 naira, 29.40 naira and 36.90 naira, respectively.
PZ Industries rose by 20 kobo to 35.70 naira, as did Flour Mills of Nigeria which closed at 10.00 naira.
Cadbury finished 15 kobo higher at 25.30 naira, the same margin as Nigerian Bottling Company which ended at 28.00 naira.

Equally buoyant were cement shares. West African Portland Cement rose 12 kobo to 30.80 naira. Benue Cement added 10 kobo to 4.68 naira, despite announcing a fall in profits during 1995. Cement Company of Northern Nigeria and Ashaka Cement rose by five kobo each to 2.73 naira and 15.40 naira.
Textile firm United Nigeria gained 10 kobo to 6.65 naira, the same as Guaranty Trust Bank which ended at 12.60 naira.
Nigerian Breweries was the major loser, ending five kobo lower at 12.90.
Traders said a large number of the shares were still flooding the market despite a favourable half-year result.
Packaging firms continued their unimpressive performance. Carnaud Metal Box dropped five kobo to 4.20 naira, Avon Crowncaps dropped two kobo to 4.50 naira and Abplast ended one kobo down at 87 kobo.
